newsitem.title: USA: Plains Resources is low-cost U.S. producer.
newsitem.headline: Plains Resources is low-cost U.S. producer.

text.p: Plains Resources Inc ranked as the most efficient U.S. oil and natural gas producer over the past three years, spending an average $2.39 per barrel of oil equivalent to replace reserves during the period, accounting firm Arthur Andersen said in an annual report released on Wednesday.

"Plains' low cost is primarily the result of its purchase of oil properties in Gulf Coast Louisiana in 1995 and additions to its California and Florida reserves in 1994 and 1995," said Victor Burk, managing director of the firm's energy practice in Houston.
Plains was trailed by majors Exxon Corp at $2.70 per boe and British Petroleum Co Plc, which averaged $2.78 per boe over the past three years to replace domestic reserves, the firm said.

Outside the United States, the success of Anadarko Petroleum Corp's Algerian exploration program made the Houston-based company the most efficient foreign producer, with an all-sources reserve replacement cost averaging $1.43 per barrel of oil equivalent (boe) over the past three years, the firm said.

Anadarko was joined by Benton Oil & Gas Co at $1.49 per boe and Chevron Corp at $2.13 per boe as the most efficient foreign producers, Arthur Andersen said in its annual report on reserve replacement in the industry.

Reserve replacement costs over the past three years from all sources -- revisions, purchases and the drill bit -- averaged $4.44 boe on U.S. production, while foreign replacement costs averaged $5.06 boe in the same period, the firm said in the report.
Arthur Andersen culled the reserve replacement costs from financial disclosures of 231 publicly held oil and gas companies to compile its 17th annual disclosure study.
